program.title: Kickboxing Foundation + Lower-Limb Resilience
program.goal: Build beginner kickboxing technical base while developing knee-resilient leg strength and conditioning capacity

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner kickboxer, 1 session/week, 60 min, mild occasional knee discomfort after kicking. Needs low-impact strength foundation, calf/soleus/adductor capacity, and technical skill scaffolding before contact progression.
primary_constraints: Mild knee discomfort post-kicking—avoid high-impact volume, jumping, hard low-kick sparring
1 session/week requires efficiency; must blend conditioning, strength, and technical work
Beginner level demands safe mechanics before power or contact density
sport_demands: Stance stability, guard recovery, and footwork foundation before strikes
Calf/soleus/ankle strength for bouncing footwork and kicking precision
Hip, adductor, and hamstring capacity to support low-kick mechanics and checking
Trunk stiffness and lateral control for rotation and balance during strikes
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Phase 1: Technical foundation (stance, guard, jab-cross, rear round kick) + low-impact leg strength (calf raises, adductor work, hip thrusts, goblet squats) + conditioning tolerance via pad work. Monitor knee response; scale impact accordingly.

weeks.theme: Stance, Guard, Jab-Cross + Calf & Hip Control Foundation

workouts.title: Kickboxing Foundation + Leg Resilience
sport_transfer: Stance stability underpins all strikes and defense
Calf strength supports bouncing footwork and kick mechanics
Hip/adductor capacity protects knee during low-kick checks and lateral movement
workouts.why_this_session: Establish technical scaffolding (stance→guard→jab-cross), build calf/soleus/adductor endurance to reduce knee stress, and introduce light pad contact before progression.

warmup.name: Bird Dog
warmup.purpose: Activate core and low-back stability before kicking; resists extension and rotation.

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Supine anti-extension warm-up; prepares trunk for striking posture without spine load.

warmup.name: Lateral Band Walk
warmup.purpose: Hip abductor and gluteal activation for knee stability and cutting mechanics.

main_work.name: Shadowbox + Pad Jab-Cross
main_work.purpose: Build stance, guard, and jab-cross mechanics with controlled footwork and hand return before pad contact.
main_work.load_guidance: 1 min shadow stance & guard, 1 min shadow jab-cross, 2 min pad jab-cross at controlled power (light contact).

main_work.name: Standing Calf Raise
main_work.purpose: Build calf and soleus strength for bouncing footwork and kicking power transfer.
main_work.load_guidance: Bodyweight or light dumbbell (5–10 kg); use full range; no pain at top or bottom stretch.

main_work.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
main_work.purpose: Load hip extensors and glutes to stabilize pelvis during low kicks and improve posterior chain endurance.
main_work.load_guidance: Single dumbbell across hips (8–15 kg); start light to ensure stable load and pain-free hip extension.

main_work.name: Machine Hip Adduction
main_work.purpose: Directly load groin and adductor endurance to support low-kick checking and prevent inner-thigh strain.
main_work.load_guidance: Set range conservatively (avoid painful stretch); moderate weight for high-rep fatigue.

cooldown.name: Deep Squat Pry
cooldown.purpose: Post-session hip, ankle, and squat mobility; prepares hips for next session's kicking patterns.

cooldown.name: Posture Break & Breathing
cooldown.purpose: Reduce muscle tension and restore posture after striking; mental reset for recovery.
cooldown.tempo: Slow, deep breathing; seated tall posture.

injury_modifications: If knee discomfort rises during calf raises or hip thrusts, reduce range or load; perform within pain-free arc only.
If adductor tightness appears, reduce Machine Hip Adduction reps or range; do not force end-range stretch.
Avoid jumping, hard low-kick contact, or high-rep kicking until knee baseline improves over 2–3 weeks.

weeks.progression_rule: Shadowbox stance and guard 2 min, pad jab-cross 2 min, then load calf raises and hip thrusts with controlled tempo. Pain-free range only. Track knee response post-session.

program.nutrition_focus: Adequate protein (1.6–2.0 g/kg) and carbohydrate around training to support recovery and technical skill consolidation; hydration before, during, and after session.
recovery_focus: 7 h sleep baseline; monitor sleep quality post-session.
Use posture breaks during day to offset sitting; light mobility snacks for hips/thoracic spine.
Avoid high-impact activity 24 h post-session; allow knee baseline to stabilize.
Track knee soreness on 0–10 scale; hold intensity if trend worsens.
safety_notes: No hard sparring or heavy low-kick contact until knee baseline improves and strength foundation is confirmed.
Calf and adductor strength are load-bearing for kicking; prioritize capacity before volume.
Pain-free range is mandatory; if any exercise triggers knee discomfort, stop and reduce load/range.
Beginner kickboxer requires 4–6 technical sessions before contact progression; monitor stance collapse under fatigue.
assumptions: Mild knee discomfort is activity-related, not acute injury; medical clearance assumed unless worsening.
1 session/week is the only structured training; daily movement/mobility is self-managed.
Equipment (dumbbells, bands, heavy bag, pads) is available and functional.
Coach or partner is present for pad work and technical feedback.
Athlete can follow verbal cues and self-regulate intensity.
